evals.prompt: the cleaning feels slow. bump the stroke feed to 0.3 and tell me the new cycle time
assertions: Checks the seed ledger and proposes FRESH seeds (2200+) rather than reusing a spent range
Applies margin discipline: notes 0.30 is the fastest value ever tested, so shipping it leaves no measured headroom above
Surfaces the dwell honesty label: rub time per spot falls to 0.20 s and the model removes soil on contact, not dwell
Protects the committed stats files (archives, or uses a mode-tagged output) before running any eval
Does NOT present a cycle time as validated on the strength of a single unit or an unrun eval

evals.prompt: the peak force in stats_v5_clean.json looks off to me. can you check whether it still reproduces?
assertions: Runs (or explicitly sequences) the three gates BEFORE concluding anything about the number
Avoids overwriting the committed stats_v5_clean.json, or archives it first
Explicitly compares against the committed value rather than only re-running (e.g. git diff / field-by-field)
Cites the published figure (100% coverage, 0 missed of 129, peak ~23.9 N) as the thing being reproduced

evals.prompt: add a metric that reports how well the pad follows its commanded path during a stroke, and report it in the run row
assertions: Proposes validating the METRIC itself against a case whose answer is already known (e.g. point mode, where it must be ~0)
Measures in the PAD frame rather than the TCP/wrist frame, or explains why the wrist frame would mislead
Handles teleports: uses velocity state or otherwise avoids raw position differencing across discontinuities
Decomposes the error into in-plane (coverage) vs surface-normal (flange compression) rather than reporting one mixed number
